title: Extend a Guardrail — The Refusals, and Why Each One Exists
note: Read these five together and the shape of the guarantee becomes clear: a contributor may make this vocabulary stricter, narrower, or larger, and may never make it looser, wider, or different. That is what lets an agent resolve a vocabulary extended by parties it has never heard of and still know the floor it was promised is intact. Two of the five are worth dwelling on. Adding a rung looks harmless — more analysis is more care — but a higher tier can mean the input travels somewhere the author never sanctioned, so it is a privacy change wearing a quality costume. And the label collision refusal is the one contributors resent most, because redefining a label is exactly what you want to do when you think the author got it wrong; the answer is that you are not wrong to want it, you are wrong to want it SILENTLY. Publish a new base version, and every verifier can see the change and choose. Every one of these is a loud load refusal rather than a quiet adjustment, because a guardrail that silently accepted a weakening would leave an operator believing in a gate that was no longer there.
